title: Ants walking over each other: does the colony stream or does it look wrong?
question: Which colony looks more like ants going about their business — and does either one look like they are cheating, standing on nothing?
context_md:
WP-9 arm 1. A living nestmate now counts as **ground** — footing only, never passability, so two ants still cannot walk through each other. It is the deliberate re-test of a dead end (775/829) whose own condition line said to re-open it "if creatures gain pass-through or climb-over".

**The numbers are not subtle.** `forage_probe seeds=8`, both arms, same seeds, median of 8:

| | off | on |
|---|---|---|
| round trips | 4 | **90.5** |
| deepest excursion | 12 | **69.5** |
| blocked / moves | 0.614 | **0.065** |
| moves | 21,870 | 21,256 |
| deliveries | 0 | 0 |

Moves are flat, so this is not "they move more" — it is that six moves in ten used to fail and now fewer than one in ten does. The jam is gone.

**What I checked before believing it, and what I could not check.** A 22x jump made me suspect the depth metric was counting ants climbing *each other* into the sky, which would be a bug wearing a result's clothes. The pictures say no — they are on the ground and on terrain, not stacked. What I cannot settle by measurement is whether it *looks* right, which is why this is here.

Two honest caveats: **deliveries are 0 in both arms**, so "deliveries held" is true but proves little — that is the separately-filed sessile-colony bug (§L), not this change. And this scene has **17 ants** where the probe has 55, so the difference you see here is milder than the numbers above.

Rendered on the `gutbias` overlay so the ants are findable at all — they are 1-2 cells each and invisible against soil otherwise. Pale = a neutral omnivore gut, which is what every ant now is.
